topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series and outlines the core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cancer as a multi-step failure of differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the core concept of cancer as a progressive failure of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture along with the experimental models used to study it.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and progression of benign to malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how benign and malignant tumors differ in invasive capacity, metastatic potential, and histological progression.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature conventions and exceptions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the systematic naming conventions and clinical exceptions used to classify neoplasms according to tissue origin and malignancy.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the physiological and anatomical mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors cause illness and patient death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence in humans and across multicellular organisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the epidemiological frequency of tumors in humans and across diverse animal taxa as a fundamental consequence of multicellular development.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the principles, histological methods, and clinical effectiveness of screening programs for early cancer detection.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reviewing the learning outcomes and framing the upcoming practical coursework.
